title: Experience Design & Domain Modelling
goal: Design how people will do their jobs with the product — flows, screens and every state — and prove it with real users. Model the business domain so the software speaks its language, respects its boundaries and enforces its rules in one place.
story: Before any code, you shape the solution: how it looks and feels, how it's structured, how data flows, and how it stays secure. In the example: a review screen for clerks, a small parsing service, and orders kept for 90 days.

definition.jtbd: Help me make sure the people who use this can do their job faster and without mistakes — including when things go wrong.

lessons.title: Prototype & Validate with Users
lessons.summary: Build prototypes of the riskiest flows and test them with real users until they work.

definition.purpose: Prove with real users that the designed flows work before anything is built.
definition.outcome: Prototypes validated against pre-set measures, with severity-rated findings fixed and retested.
definition.jtbd: Help me know the design works for the people who will use it, not just for us.
exit: Measures met in the latest round
No open severity 1–2 findings

Build the prototype at the lowest fidelity that answers them
Plan the round and set thresholds

alternates: Coded prototype on real data where realism decides the result (e.g. parsing confidence)
Remote unmoderated test for simple tasks
edgeCases: Expert users who will tolerate a poor design
Users at two sites working differently
exceptions: Too few participants → extra round, confidence noted
failures: Thresholds moved after seeing results
Prototype so polished that stakeholders treat it as finished

routing.forward: Validated prototype & findings → 3.1.3 Specify UI & States

rules: No moving the thresholds after the round

lessons.title: Specify UI & States

definition.jtbd: Help me build the screen right first time, including what users see when things go wrong.

Fill the state matrix and write the microcopy

Existing screen changed → spec only the delta
edgeCases: Asynchronous step where the result arrives later
Stale data from a nightly copy of master data
exceptions: Architecture changes failure behaviour late → re-spec the affected states

Messages that blame the user or hide what was kept

lessons.title: Design for Accessibility
lessons.summary: Make the design meet WCAG 2.2 AA and work with assistive technology before it is built.

definition.purpose: Make sure everyone who must use the product can — by design, not by later repair.
definition.outcome: A design that meets WCAG 2.2 AA, checked by keyboard, screen reader and contrast tools, with evidence per criterion.

exceptions: No assistive-technology user available → specialist walkthrough, flagged

processes.title: Domain Modelling
processes.summary: Ubiquitous language, bounded contexts, entities, aggregates and invariants.

definition.purpose: Model the business domain so the software speaks its language, respects its boundaries and enforces its rules in one place.
definition.outcome: An agreed glossary, a context map with owners, a domain model per context, and testable invariants and business rules.
definition.jtbd: Help me make sure the system's things and rules are the business's things and rules — and that each rule lives in exactly one place.
exit: Glossary and context map agreed
Domain model reviewed
Every invariant testable and assigned to one aggregate

dependencies: Session notes and workflow maps from DISCOVER
flow.stateTransitions: Unexplored → Language agreed → Contexts mapped → Modelled → Rules verified

cases.happyPath: One Event Storming workshop, a clear context map and small aggregates with testable rules.
alternates: Simple CRUD context → light model
Existing model → extend it
edgeCases: One PDF holding several orders
Same word meaning different things at two sites
exceptions: Expert unsure of a rule → provisional rule with a review date
failures: Model built from technical layers, not the business
Rules that live only in clerks' heads

routing.forward: Domain model, context map & invariant catalogue → 3.3 Architecture Definition and 3.4 Data Design
routing.alternate: Generic subdomain → buy and wrap behind an adapter
routing.escalation: Ownership dispute between teams → design authority
routing.stop: No new model needed → record and skip — recorded in the learning log

criteria: One meaning per term per context
rules: Use the domain's words in UI, code and tests
policies: Glossary is the single source of terms

decisions: Where the boundaries are and which rules the system enforces

agents: AI assistant for transcribing workshops and drafting examples
roles: C — Domain experts, QA lead, ERP team
execution.authority: Domain experts own meanings and rules; the architect owns the model; the design authority settles ownership disputes.
